title: Frontier results, on device - RL Nabors, Arize
talk_summary: Arize's RL Nabors argues you should prototype with a frontier model to prove a task is possible, then build a golden eval set and test progressively smaller/cheaper models to find the 'smallest and good enough' (SAGE) model, closing the gap with prompt engineering and post-processing. She demonstrates on a thread-summarization feature that a 3B Llama with few-shot prompting plus harness post-processing matched Claude Sonnet on accuracy and latency at zero marginal inference cost.

takeaways.technique: Prototype big, deploy small (SAGE model selection)
takeaways.what_they_do: Prove the task is possible with the largest model, define success criteria on a golden set, then test from smallest to largest model and pick the smallest that clears the bar rather than the one engineers recommend.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You're going to want to select the smallest model that gives acceptable responses for your use case.
takeaways.numbers: Llama 3.2 3B hit ~90% accuracy vs Claude Sonnet baseline; Gemma 4 was ~8s latency vs Llama ~1s

takeaways.technique: Golden dataset + capability eval before model swap
takeaways.what_they_do: Curate human-checked input/output pairs (JSONL), define measurable criteria (JSON parse, structural validity, factual consistency, length, P50/P95 latency), and run every candidate model against the same set, opening raw outputs to inspect disagreements.
takeaways.evidence_quote: A golden data set is a curated high-quality collection of preferably human-labeled input-output pairs that you're going to use as the ground truth
takeaways.numbers: 28 examples (14 threads x 2 output styles) were enough to rank 4 models

takeaways.what_they_do: When Claude judged Llama's output it favored its sibling; inspecting raw evals revealed the 'gap' was judge strictness, and deterministic post-processing (truncation, reference-count checks) closed the rest.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Claude was favoring its little sister... this is why it's important to crack them open.
takeaways.numbers: Post-processing took JSON validity and structural validity to 100%

takeaways.what_they_do: Test prompt variants isolating one change each (reformatted input, few-shot, strict negative rules, chain-of-thought) and measure each against the eval criteria.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The best performing one was the few shot one that provided a couple of threads and a couple of examples.
takeaways.numbers: Few-shot: +200ms latency, better length/accuracy; strict negative rules made it worse; CoT +600ms

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep the eval suite running like CI/CD tests so prompt or model upgrades don't silently degrade output.

takeaways.technique: Route by task difficulty, not by habit
takeaways.what_they_do: Audit what is actually being sent to frontier models and ask whether a smaller model could handle it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: how many Claude calls could be Llama calls?
takeaways.numbers: Author cut ~$1/day of inference to zero marginal cost on-device
